instruction: Mirror the yellow triangle by flipping it horizontally to the other side of the canvas.

metadata.explanation: Task requires flipping the yellow triangle horizontally. The evaluator exports the image and checks if the triangle centroid is now on the right side of the canvas (indicating successful horizontal flip from left to right).

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all requirements - triangle is detected (yellow color), moved to opposite side, actually flipped/mirrored (not just moved), and maintains shape/size.

Correct flip verification: The verify_horizontal_flip() function properly checks that pixels at (y, x) map to (y, width - 1 - x), confirming actual horizontal mirroring occurred, not just repositioning.

Robust triangle detection: Uses color thresholding with yellow RGB ranges (R>180, G>180, B<100) with fallback to lenient thresholds, correctly identifies yellow pixels instead of making fragile assumptions.
Three-layer validation: Check 1 ensures triangle moved to opposite side; Check 2 verifies pixel-level mirroring with 80% match threshold; Check 3 confirms shape/size maintained (90% tolerance).
Proper state extraction: Getter retrieves both result and original images for comparison, enabling before/after verification of the flip operation.
Good edge case handling: Handles None values, dimension mismatches, missing files, color tolerance for compression artifacts, and samples up to 1000 pixels for performance.
Semantic correctness: Logic flow is sound - detect yellow in both images, compare centroids to verify side change, verify pixel mirroring to confirm flip (not move), check size preservation.
